analysis:
All three changed files are docs only, and no source or enforcement code is in the diff, so I found no security regression. I could not check these claims against code.

1. docs/reference/configuration.md (head 320-323): adds four DARKBLOOM_NEMOTRON_SUPER_* variables (MTP opt-in, depth 1-3, verification mode, max concurrent 1-64). All are default-off or restrictive, and the docs say they are not forwarded to LaunchAgents. Claims to verify in the code (TB-007/T-010/T-029): the MTP owner refuses media, invalid values fail the load, and concurrency above one with MTP fails the load. Relevant to T-028 (residual GPU data) and T-029.

2. docs/reference/nemotron-super-image-formats.md (new): documents an in-process PNG decoder and an ImageIO JPEG decode of consumer-supplied inline images, inside the provider process that holds decrypted prompts (A-001, TB-003/TB-007, ADV-002).
- Claimed hardening: encoded bytes capped at min(MediaIngest limit, 64 MiB) and an 8 MiB request body; pixel and axis caps checked before any raster allocation; 500-scan limit; CRC checks; a 1 MiB text/ICC inflate cap; a decoder memory quote plus a 256 MiB workspace; a 2.09 GB tower reservation.
- The doc itself says ImageIO decode cannot be cancelled, which has T-010 and T-029 implications.
- The doc says the owner is unregistered, so no production exposure is claimed. The threat model has no explicit entry for the image-decoder parsing surface. T-050 covers video temp files, not images. If the owner is registered later, add or extend a threat entry and review the decoder code, which this PR does not supply.

3. docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md (line 186): adds that a cold result returns only after the attempt's host IO refund completes. This tightens the T-041 staging-reservation lifetime and has no negative effect.

The threat model needs no change for these doc edits. The decoder and MTP code should be reviewed separately.
